headline: Cell-state reference atlases expand as models infer cell-type-resolved gene regulation
label: Cell Atlases And Regulatory Inference
summary: TISCH3, LACA and CellStressDB, plus preprints such as AlphaGenome 2 and DRAFT, push regulatory analysis toward cell-type and cell-state resolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is regulatory analysis at cell-type and cell-state resolution, backed by larger integrated references. TISCH3 reaches 477 tumour-microenvironment datasets, including 69 spatial collections. A pan-cancer lncRNA atlas of 370,000+ cells links lncRNAs to regulons, CRISPR screens and survival. LACA spans single-cell data from 134 species annotated with maximum lifespans, and CellStressDB curates 131 physical-stress studies. On the modelling side, AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-conditioned regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb sequence. DRAFT infers dynamic GRNs along single-cell multi-omics trajectories. A TNBC framework combining Perturb-seq CRISPRi responses with ENCODE TF-binding priors outperforms GENIE3. Assays widen the available inputs: TrES-seq pairs scRNA-seq with two histone marks, and COMET assigns bulk long reads to cell types by methylation. HIT-Fuse addresses multimodal fusion with missing modalities, and SpaceMACE addresses spatial tumour-cell annotation. The items do not show how these references support cross-cohort validation.
